# howtf.io

> Systems-engineering deep dives by Deep Shah. Every post reconstructs a real
> production failure from the bottom of the stack (linkers, loaders, RDMA,
> GPUDirect, Linux memory management), verifies the mechanism against public
> source with pinned commits, and ships a runnable reproducer.

Topics: RDMA, InfiniBand, libibverbs, GPUDirect, NCCL, ELF, linkers, dynamic
loading, Linux kernel, fork(), memory registration, GPU training
infrastructure, production debugging.

## Posts

- [howtf does ./app reach main()?](https://howtf.io/blog/ELF-Linking-101/):
  the life of a command from execve to main(), through the kernel, ld.so, and
  the PLT/GOT. Linking & Loading, Part 1.
- [howtf can a device be both present and not found?](https://howtf.io/blog/split-state-linking/):
  an RDMA device visible to one library and invisible to another in the same
  process. Names the failure class "split-state linking". Linking & Loading,
  Part 2.
- [howtf did a four-byte buffer crash the checkpoint worker?](https://howtf.io/blog/four-bytes-one-page/):
  a GPUDirect RDMA visibility fence, ibv_fork_init's MADV_DONTFORK page
  rounding, and fork children segfaulting on memory the parent could read.

## Topic hubs

- [RDMA deep dives](https://howtf.io/topics/rdma/): all RDMA/InfiniBand posts.

## Reproducers

- [Demo code](https://github.com/dshah133/howtf/tree/main/demo): container-based
